10.1002_adfm.78997: We demonstrate the electronic structure engineering of iron antimony oxide (FeSbO 4 , FSO) through heteroatom (Ti, Zn) doping and controlled oxygen vacancy formation for efficient electrocatalytic water splitting. Heteroatom incorporation elevates intrinsic electrical conductivity to accelerate charge transfer during the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Simultaneously, surface oxygen vacancies polarize the local electronic environment at Fe active sites, optimizing the adsorption energetics of oxygen‐containing intermediates to significantly boost oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance. Ti‐doped FSO with moderate oxygen vacancies (TFSO 30 ) achieves outstanding HER activity (300 mV at 50 mA/cm 2 , Tafel slope of 119.38 mV/dec) due to vacancy‐induced electronic modulation. In contrast, higher oxygen vacancy concentration (TFSO 60 ) drives superior OER performance (188 mV at 50 mA/cm 2 , Tafel slope of 76.18 mV/dec) compared to IrO 2, primarily driven by charge redistribution and the generation of high‐valence active metal species. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that Ti doping and oxygen vacancies synergistically tune the electronic structure, promote charge transport, and lower reaction energy barriers to accelerate overall water‐splitting kinetics. Overall, this work highlights Ti‐doped FSO as an efficient, earth‐abundant electrocatalyst and provides useful insights into defect‐engineering strategies for catalytic energy conversion.
10.1002_aenm.202600012: Electric double‐layer capacitors (EDLCs), which store energy via reversible ion adsorption and desorption at the electrode‐electrolyte interface, hold considerable promise for energy storage under extreme temperature conditions. However, their practical application faces significant limitations associated with temperature‐dependent limitations: at high‐temperature, electrolyte decomposition can reduce Coulombic efficiency or triggers device failure, whereas at low‐temperature, diminished ionic conductivity or electrolyte crystallization leads to performance deterioration or functional breakdown. A comprehensive understanding of these constraints is therefore essential for designing EDLCs capable of operating reliably in extreme environments. This review begins with a systematic overview of the working principles and practical applications of EDLCs, followed by a comparative analysis of various electrolytes, highlighting their respective advantages and shortcomings. Subsequently, we outline specific design principles for both electrolytes and electrodes based on key physicochemical properties and summarize recent advances in high‐temperature, low‐temperature, and wide‐temperature EDLCs. Finally, forward‐looking perspectives and strategic directions are proposed to guide the development of next‐generation EDLCs capable of delivering stable performance under extreme temperatures. This review aims to provide critical insights and rational design guidelines to advance EDLC technology for demanding, extreme‐environment applications.
10.1039_d5ta05225d: A highly sensitive hybrid nanogenerator with a mycelium network-inspired piezoelectric mat, combined with Maxwell's displacement current, enables underwater wireless signalling for a Morse code-supported battery-free aquatic rescue system.
